title: Stars, hexagons and kites from Daud Sutton
subtitle: Daud Sutton, Islamic Design, page 27

construction.note: The finished design was read from Brian Wichmann’s DS3 drawing, its corners snapped to exact values. We devised the construction: one circle from K1 fixes the star’s square at G, and every other line comes from G and the cell. The drawing gives no steps.
construction.changes: The compass steps, their order and the named points are ours. The comparison with the drawing checks the finished lines, not how the design was first laid out. No photo of a building was checked: the source gives no place.

credits.source: Tiling Search, data184/DS3: Daud Sutton, page 27 (left)
credits.creator: Brian Wichmann
credits.note: The design was read from his drawing. He takes it from Daud Sutton, Islamic Design: A Genius for Geometry (Wooden Books, 2007), page 27 (left), which gives no place. The construction is ours.

given.O: The centre of an eight-pointed star.
given.A: Halfway from O to the side of the square tile on the horizontal line.

steps.text: Draw a horizontal straight line through O and A. Draw a circle with centre O through A.

Draw a vertical line through O. The two lines cross the circle at A, B, C and D. Draw a vertical line through each of A and B. Draw a horizontal line through each of C and D. These lines make the square cell, with corners K1, K2, K3 and K4. Draw a straight line through O and K1.
steps.textWithoutHelpers: Draw a vertical line through O. The two lines cross the circle at A, B, C and D. Draw a vertical line through A. Draw a horizontal line through C. They cross at K1, a corner of the cell. Draw a straight line through O and K1.

steps.text: Draw a circle with centre K1 through A. It crosses the line from O to K1 at G. Draw a vertical line through G. Turn it round O by 90°, three times. The four lines make the square of the star at O.
Draw a straight line through A and C. Draw a circle with centre O through G. It crosses the horizontal line at T. Draw a line through T parallel to line AC. Turn it round O by 90°, three times.
steps.textWithoutHelpers: Draw a circle with centre O through G. It crosses the horizontal line at T. Draw a line through T at 45° to the horizontal line. Turn it round O by 90°, three times.

steps.text: The line through T crosses the vertical line through A at M, above the horizontal line. Draw a line through M parallel to line AC. Turn it round O by 90°, three times.
steps.textWithoutHelpers: The line through T crosses the vertical line through A at M, above the horizontal line. Draw a line through M parallel to the line through T. Turn it round O by 90°, three times.

steps.text: The circle crosses the line from O to K1 at E. Draw a horizontal line through E. It crosses the line through M at P. Draw a vertical line through P. Turn it round O by 90°, three times. The lines make the small stars at the corners.
steps.textWithoutHelpers: The circle crosses the line from O to K1 at E. The horizontal line through E crosses the line through M at P. Draw a vertical line through P. Turn it round O by 90°, three times. The lines make the small stars at the corners.

steps.text: Join K1, K2, K3 and K4 to mark the tile that repeats.

ink.text: Ink the star at O, the small stars at the corners and the long lines between them. They close the hexagons, the kites and the triangles.

pattern.text: Put copies of the square cell side by side. A large star sits in the middle and a small star at every corner.
